highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219: Claude Opus 5 Now Default with 1M Context
highlights.summary: The latest release adds Claude Opus 5 as the new default Opus model, offering a massive 1M token context window at $10/$50 per million tokens in fast mode. It also introduces `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` to automatically deny non-allowlisted hosts without prompting, tightening security for sandboxed commands. If you're running long sessions or security-sensitive workflows, this update is well worth installing.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.218: /code-review Now Runs as Background Subagent
highlights.summary: The `/code-review` slash command now runs as a background subagent, meaning review output no longer clutters your main conversation thread. It also correctly targets stacked slash commands as its review scope, making it much more useful in complex multi-step workflows. This is a quality-of-life improvement for anyone who regularly uses code review inside Claude Code.

highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic officially announced Claude Opus 5, their most capable model to date, featuring a 1 million token context window and improved performance on complex coding and reasoning tasks. This is the model now powering Claude Code's default Opus tier, making long-context agentic coding sessions significantly more capable. Beginners and advanced users alike should read the announcement to understand what's now possible.

highlights.title: Anthropic Runs Large-Scale Code Migrations with Claude Code
highlights.summary: Anthropic has published a blog post detailing how they use Claude Code internally to perform large-scale code migrations across their own codebase. The article offers practical insight into how agentic AI can handle repetitive, high-volume refactoring tasks that would take human engineers weeks. If you're considering using Claude Code for migrations or refactoring at work, this is a must-read case study.

highlights.title: Claude Code Tutorial for Non-Coders
highlights.summary: This YouTube tutorial is aimed at people with little to no coding experience who want to use Claude Code to build projects. It walks through the basics of setting up and prompting Claude Code in plain language, making it one of the most accessible entry points for newcomers. If you're just getting started, this is a great first video to watch before diving into more advanced guides.

highlights.title: Mastering Claude Code in 30 Minutes
highlights.summary: This concise YouTube video promises to take you from beginner to confident Claude Code user in under half an hour, covering core workflows and productivity shortcuts. It's ideal for developers who already have some coding experience and want a fast, dense overview rather than a slow step-by-step guide. Bookmark this one for a Saturday morning skill boost.

highlights.title: Setting Up a Spare Mac for Claude Code to Control: Step-by-Step Guide
highlights.summary: This guide walks you through configuring a secondary Mac so Claude Code can operate it autonomously, essentially turning a spare machine into a dedicated AI coding agent. It covers the setup steps needed for remote control and sandboxed operation, which is useful for running long agentic tasks without interrupting your main workstation. Advanced users looking to scale their Claude Code usage to a second machine will find this immediately practical.

highlights.title: Cognikernel: Local Persistent Memory for Claude Code Sessions
highlights.summary: Cognikernel is an open-source tool that gives Claude Code a persistent local memory store, so architectural decisions and context from previous sessions are available in future ones — without relying solely on CLAUDE.md files. This solves a common frustration where each new Claude Code session starts with no knowledge of prior work. Developers who work on long-running projects will find this a meaningful upgrade to their workflow.

tips_of_the_day: Use the new `/code-review` background subagent to get a full review without losing your place in a conversation — trigger it at the end of a feature session and let it run while you write your commit message.

If you work across multiple projects, maintain a separate CLAUDE.md per repository with key architectural decisions and naming conventions baked in — Claude Code reads it on startup and will immediately have the context it needs without you repeating yourself.

Take advantage of Claude Opus 5's 1M token context window by feeding in entire module directories at once when debugging cross-file issues — instead of asking Claude to look at one file at a time, let it see the full picture and identify root causes faster.
